awards.title: King Charles III Coronation Medal
awards.summary: Awarded by The Duke of Edinburgh’s Award for exemplary volunteer service.

awards.title: Report on Business Best Executive 2021
awards.summary: Mona Malone has navigated multiple ups and downs in her 25-year career with BMO. So despite the challenges of COVID-19, she still managed to be a steadfast presence for her team. “In any time of crisis, there’s an opportunity and a need for leadership,” Malone says. “The health and safety of our people was of paramount importance.” The bank launched multiple new offerings during the pandemic, including a virtual healthcare app, a daily stipend for workers who had to work from the office, 15 extra lieu days for pandemic-related matters and regular call-in sessions with mental-health experts. Malone says she’s guided by the adage “People will forget what you say or do, but they won’t forget how you made them feel.” That was particularly important over the past year. “I know that how we listened was so important, and would be something they would remember long after the pandemic was over,” she says.

Enrich person.summary:
Mona is a results-oriented senior leader who is passionate in building strong, engaged and high-performing teams.

She currently services as Chief Administrative Officer, and Chief Human Resources Officer of BMO Financial Group. She oversees Human Resources, Marketing, Communications & Social Impact, Corporate Real, Procurement and BMO Québec. Mona is also a member of BMO’s Executive Committee and U.S. Management Committee.

With more than two decades of experience in the financial services industry, Mona has long been a passionate advocate for the power of purpose and culture in driving sustained performance.

Mona is also deeply committed to being actively involved in the community. For over 25 years she’s been involved with youth-based charities and is a recipient of the Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal and King Charles III Coronation Medal for exemplary community service.

She also serves as the Chair of the Advisory Council for the Ian O. Ihnatowycz Institute for Leadership at the Ivey Business School, Board member of the Branksome Hall Board of Governors and a member of The Long Run Institute Board of Governors.

Enrich person.summary:
With nearly two decades of experience in the banking industry, I bring a strong track record of strategic leadership, talent development, and business growth. In my current role as Director of Workforce Development Programs at BMO U.S., I lead high-impact initiatives that support colleague development, strengthen team culture, and prepare future leaders across key segments of the organization.
Previously, as National Sales Manager, I led efforts to expand market presence and deepen corporate partnerships, driving profitability and positioning BMO as a trusted financial partner. My career has spanned roles from Licensed Banker to National Sales Leader, including the design of a retail sales training program for a multi-bank holding company.
My passion for Business Banking was solidified during my time as a Business Banker and later as Head of Business Banking Sales, where I led transformational growth and built high-performing teams. I thrive on leading through change, mentoring others, and creating scalable solutions that deliver measurable impact.
I’m energized by opportunities that challenge me to think differently, lead boldly, and contribute to meaningful outcomes—for our clients, our teams, and the communities we serve.
